title: Indian Laurel Fig: Ancient Banyans You Can Visit
meta_description: Hong Kong keeps a tree category almost nowhere else does: stone wall trees, growing out of masonry and looked after by the buildings department.
intro: Hong Kong keeps a category of tree that almost nowhere else bothers with. A stone wall tree grows straight out of a masonry retaining wall, roots threaded down through the joints, and the department responsible for several of them is not the one that runs the parks but the one that looks after government masonry. Twenty-seven of them line three walls on Forbes Street, and when engineers planned to extend the MTR through Kennedy Town the station was rerouted rather than the wall removed. The species is common enough that the city plants it by the thousand and almost never lets one grow old. The exception is the King Banyan in Kowloon Park, put at four hundred years and still the largest urban tree in the city after a 2007 typhoon took a third of its trunk. Eight mapped, in Hong Kong, Malaga and Seville.
